cim: University of Indianapolis receives $8.5 million grant to expand artificial intelligence programs - WISH-TV
cim_eredeti: University of Indianapolis receives $8.5 million grant to expand artificial intelligence programs - WISH-TV
szoveg_eredeti:
INDIANAPOLIS— The University of Indianapolis has received an $8.5 million grant from Lilly Endowment Inc. to establish a new artificial intelligence center and expand AI education across its campus.

The funding will support the creation of the Center for Artificial Intelligence for Human Performance, along with major investments in academic programs, faculty training and technology infrastructure.

The three-year initiative is expected to begin in January and will focus on preparing students for careers increasingly influenced by artificial intelligence while helping Indiana businesses and nonprofit organizations adopt the technology.

“Artificial intelligence is fundamentally changing the way we live and work at breathtaking speeds,” University of Indianapolis President Tanuja Singh said in a statement. “Higher education has a responsibility to prepare students not just to use these new tools, but to think critically about how and why they are used.”

Under the initiative, the university plans to create or revise as many as 330 courses to incorporate artificial intelligence into the curriculum. The school will also develop nine AI-focused micro-credentials and provide students with opportunities to work on industry-sponsored projects.

Faculty members will receive additional training and resources to incorporate AI into their teaching, with an emphasis on critical thinking, ethical decision-making and responsible use of the technology.

The university also plans to introduce AI-powered tools to improve academic advising, student support services, transfer credit evaluations and data security.

The new center will be located in a renovated section of Krannert Memorial Library on the university’s campus.

University officials say the center will serve two primary purposes: encouraging discussions about the relationship between artificial intelligence and human performance, and providing practical assistance to businesses and nonprofit organizations.

Small businesses and nonprofits that lack the resources or expertise to implement AI independently will be able to access customized consulting services through the center.

“The Center for Artificial Intelligence for Human Performance is particularly exciting because it pairs the expertise of our faculty and the creative energy and problem-solving abilities of our students to address the real-world challenges facing Hoosier businesses and organizations,” UIndy Provost Chris Plouff said.

Plouff said the initiative will also give students valuable experience applying classroom lessons to real-world problems.

“Our students will benefit greatly from the hands-on experience they gain by applying what they learn in the classroom,” Plouff said. “Our entire state will benefit from new ideas and practical solutions.”

The grant is part of Lilly Endowment’s Artificial Intelligence in Higher Education initiative, which is providing funding to 35 Indiana colleges and universities.

The initiative is designed to help higher education institutions respond to the growing influence of artificial intelligence and prepare students, faculty and staff for technological changes in the workplace and everyday life.

The University of Indianapolis has already begun exploring the technology’s impact through events such as its inaugural AI Summit in April, which brought together business leaders, educators, technology experts and policymakers.

The university plans to hold another AI Summit in fall 2027.

Singh said the investment will help the university expand its educational mission while ensuring that students understand the broader implications of artificial intelligence.

“We must ensure that technology serves people, not the other way around,” Singh said.
